title: Campaign
description: A named workspace grouping related audiences and deliveries. There is no audience_ids[] field — audiences[] (below) is the only audience-linkage field the handler ever returns.

description.description: User-authored campaign brief, intended market, goals, and constraints.

audiences.description: Audiences linked to this campaign — expanded on GET /v1/campaigns/{id}; empty array on list responses.

segment_ids.description: IDs of include-role segments in this audience.

excluded_segment_ids.description: IDs of exclude-role segments in this audience.

segments.description: Constituent segments; audiences can combine multiple subtypes.

excluded_segments.description: Expanded summaries of the exclude-role segments, same semantics as `segments`.

linked_at.description: When this audience was linked to the campaign.

ExpandedSegment.description: Constituent segment summary and saved filter definition. Audiences may combine multiple segment subtypes; there is no primary segment or audience subtype.

record_count.description: Cached record count of the segment. Null if never counted.

input_record_count.description: matched subtype only. Count of records in the uploaded identity file. Null otherwise.

match_count.description: matched subtype only. Count of records successfully matched. Null otherwise.

Filter.description: A single filter condition for audience discovery or job execution

field.description: Canonical catalog field_name (e.g. age or state). ZIP5 also accepts zip, zip_code, or postal_code as input aliases; saved responses use zip5.

text_comparison.description: Optional STRING comparison mode for =, !=, IN, NOT IN, and LIKE, or ARRAY<STRING> membership mode for ARRAY_CONTAINS and ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY. Defaults to exact. Case-insensitive mode applies Unicode case folding to both the stored value and the supplied value.

trim_whitespace.description: Optionally trim leading and trailing whitespace on both sides of a STRING or ARRAY<STRING> comparison. Defaults to false; independent of text_comparison.

value.description: The value to match against. For state, a published two-letter code or full State name is accepted and normalized to the code. Scalar types (`string`, `number`, `boolean`) are used for single-value operators (`=`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `LIKE`, `ARRAY_CONTAINS`). Pass an **array** for `IN`, `NOT IN`, and `ARRAY_CONTAINS_ANY` — pass the array directly with no comma-encoding. `BETWEEN` takes a two-element array `[low, high]`. Omit entirely for `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` checks.

FilterGroup.description:
A group of Filter conditions. All `filters` within a single group are **always ANDed together** — there is no per-group intra-operator. The `combinator` attribute is an **inter-group** operator: it controls how this group is joined to the immediately preceding group in the array. The `combinator` on the first group (index 0) is always ignored.

Example — `(city = "NYC" AND state = "NY") OR (state = "CA")`:
```json [
  { "id": "g1", "filters": [{"field":"city","op":"=","value":"NYC"},
                            {"field":"state","op":"=","value":"NY"}],
    "combinator": "AND" },
  { "id": "g2", "filters": [{"field":"state","op":"=","value":"CA"}],
    "combinator": "OR" }
] ```
Group g1's `combinator` is irrelevant (it is the first group). Group g2's `combinator: "OR"` means the result is `(g1) OR (g2)`.

id.description: Stable identifier (UUID or NanoID). Used to track groups across edits.

filters.description: One or more filter conditions. All conditions in this array are combined with AND. Provide at least one filter per group.

combinator.description: **Inter-group operator.** Joins this group to the previous group in the array. `AND` narrows the result; `OR` broadens it. Ignored on the first group (index 0) — that group has no predecessor to join.
